t39_U1: Sometimes the urge to get away from what's coming up gets a lot bigger. All of a sudden you need a drink, or that ex doesn't seem so bad after all. Some people start a whole new business. If that's you, it might mean you got close to something that really hurts, and that's kind of progress, honestly! I'd thank whatever part of you came up with the escape plan.
t39_U2: That part with the escape plan is guarding something that hurts. It's why I'm careful about pushing into intensive meditation or psychedelic plant medicine before there's enough Nurturer and Protector in you. Getting past guards like that is kind of what those tools are for, and I get the appeal. They can just get there before there's a grown-up big enough to hold whatever comes through, and then your little one is out in the open with nobody there yet.
t39_U3a: Your own history with psychedelics and other drugs counts here too, more than anybody's trip report. If something ever gave you a psychotic kind of reaction, like voices or paranoia, I wouldn't take it again without a professional assessment, even if you've felt totally fine since. I know that sounds strict for one time. Same if you kept seeing things after it should've worn off. A reaction like that says something about how your own mind handles those states, so I'd be careful with anything else that messes with your sense of what's real, too. That doesn't make every drug dangerous for you, though.
t39_U3b: Milder reactions count too, like getting confused or spaced out again and again (not the fun kind of spaced out). If one of these reactions ever gets severe, or you can't tell whether you're safe, get professional help right away. And if it keeps coming back when you're sober, even mildly, get it looked at. Maybe you start to suspect a prescribed medicine is part of the problem, or something your body's come to depend on. I'd still never just stop it cold. Coming off some things too fast is dangerous in itself, so get a doctor's help with that.
t39_U4: Gentle meditation or self-hypnosis is a different story. It can really calm your nervous system down, so the guards often ease off on their own, slowly enough for the grown-up in you to keep up. A lot of people find that a mantra they feel some heart connection to, repeated in their head or out loud, especially with a nice melody, can lower the walls enough for the heart to open up. It's not something to lean on all day as a way of coping, but used as therapy it can be super effective.
